text.p: These are the leading stories in the Mozambican press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Peasants in northern Mozambique are refusing to sell their maize surpluses because local traders have cut the purchase price following a drop in the price on the international market. The peasants are said to be hoping for a better price from the World Food Programme if food is needed for conflict victims in other countries.

- The first business mission from Singapore to visit Mozambique since independence in 1975 held a meeting on Monday with Mozambican entrepreneurs to identify areas of possible cooperation -- particularly agriculture, fisheries, the textile and chemical industries, mining and trade.

- The reincarnation of Maguiguana Cossa, a resistance hero killed by the Portuguese 100 years ago, was briefed on the present Mozambican government's policies by Culture Minister Mateus Katupha at a village ceremony marking the anniversary this week. Local elders insisted on the meeting, claiming that the warrior's spirit had possessed a 30-year local woman.
